problem: End-to-end CNN+RNN agents trained only on reward perform poorly on ObjectNav: the Habitat 2020 DD-PPO baseline reaches just 6.2% test-std success because of overfitting and sample inefficiency. This pushed the state of the art toward modular pipelines that build explicit semantic maps and use analytic planners, such as SemExp.
motivation: In PointNav, a generic CNN+RNN scaled with RL, plus auxiliary tasks, beats map-based methods. ObjectNav differs because the agent cannot use GPS as a progress signal toward the goal, so it must learn to explore. The authors ask whether generic representation-learning objectives (auxiliary tasks) and an exploration objective can restore a map-free learned agent, and they want to understand how such agents work internally (behaviour, probes, RNN dynamics).
key_idea: Train a map-free, split-belief CNN+GRU agent on ObjectNav using three things: semantic inputs (segmentation plus a 'goal fraction in view' scalar), extra self-supervised auxiliary tasks (inverse dynamics and coverage prediction), and a decaying visitation-based exploration reward. A 'tethered' second policy head then learns the sparse ObjectNav reward off-policy to improve efficiency.
insight: Generic auxiliary tasks and exploration signals are enough to bring an end-to-end agent to state-of-the-art ObjectNav success; explicit maps are not required. The single most important input is the Semantic Goal Exists (SGE) feature: removing it drops VAL SR from 34.4 to 20.3. Supplying SGE as an auxiliary target instead of an input is even worse (17.7). Removing all auxiliary tasks gives 30.4 SR / 6.56 SPL versus 34.4 / 9.58, and each new auxiliary task adds roughly 1-2 points (coverage prediction is the largest). Tethered sparse-reward training preserves success better than directly fine-tuning on the sparse reward (26.6/9.79 vs 23.1/8.43). The analysis suggests agents simplify their inputs to keep RNN dynamics stable: the 6-action agent stares at the floor and is therefore more fragile to noisy RedNet segmentation. Fixed-point analysis indicates that auxiliary tasks shorten memory spans, i.e. constrain effective RNN dimensionality, which may explain how they reduce overfitting.
method: Split-belief agent (from Ye et al. 2020 PointNav): RGBD is downsampled to 240x320; the semantic channel is embedded into 4 dimensions; a ResNet18 encodes vision and the goal ID is embedded to 32 dimensions. These are concatenated with GPS+Compass and SGE, fed to several independent GRUs ('beliefs', hidden size 196, one per auxiliary task), fused by observation-conditioned attention, and passed to a linear actor-critic head.

Semantic inputs: semantic segmentation (ground truth from MP3D during training; at test, predicted by a RedNet pretrained on SUN RGB-D and fine-tuned on 100k MP3D views for the 21 goal classes). SGE is a scalar giving the fraction of the frame occupied by the goal category.

Reward shaping: r_success = 2.5, slack = -1e-4 per step, plus an exploration term 0.25·d^t/v. The exploration term rewards visiting 2.5m voxels, decays with the visit count v, and decays with episode time (d = 0.995).

Six auxiliary tasks: CPC|A at k=4 and k=16 and PBL at k=8 (from prior work), plus three new ones. Action Distribution Prediction (ADP) predicts the action distribution via KL at k=6. Generalized Inverse Dynamics (GID) uses a GRU to decode individual actions from h_t and φ_{t+k} at k=4. Coverage Prediction (CP) uses a GRU conditioned on belief and visit count to predict the number of new voxels at each of the next 16 steps.

Tethered policy: a second actor-critic head on the shared fused belief is trained with the sparse success reward only. It uses V-trace-style clipped importance weights inside PPO (clip a=0.01, b=1.0). The exploration-reward policy acts first; the tethered policy acts for the final 25M frames.

Training: PPO+GAE with Adam, about 125M frames (8 GPU-weeks) per agent, 5-6M parameters. A 3D GPS is used in training and a 2D GPS at evaluation. Agents are optionally fine-tuned for about 10M frames on RedNet segmentation to close the GT-to-predicted gap. Both 4-action and 6-action (with look up/down) suites are trained.

Analysis tools: manual failure-mode coding, linear probes (time, max SGE, room, distance to goal), belief-vs-observation curvature correlation, and fixed-point Jacobian eigen-analysis to measure RNN memory spans.

setting.backbone: ResNet18 + multiple GRU belief modules with attention fusion and linear actor-critic (trained from scratch with PPO); RedNet (SUN RGB-D pretrained, MP3D fine-tuned) for test-time semantic segmentation
setting.model_size: 5-6M parameters (excluding auxiliary modules); GRU hidden size 196
setting.training_data: MP3D ObjectNav train split (Habitat Challenge 2020, 21 goal categories). About 125M frames of RL per agent (8 GPU-weeks), using ground-truth MP3D semantic segmentation during training. Optional extra 10M frames of fine-tuning with RedNet predictions. RedNet fine-tuned on 100K rendered MP3D views.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + GPS+Compass (3D in training, 2D at eval) + goal category ID + semantic segmentation (GT in training, RedNet-predicted at test) + SGE scalar
setting.action_space: discrete: MOVE_FORWARD, TURN_LEFT, TURN_RIGHT, LOOK_UP, LOOK_DOWN, STOP (6-action) or a 4-action variant without look up/down; 500-step limit
setting.privileged: none at test time for the reported challenge numbers (segmentation predicted by RedNet; noiseless GPS+Compass per the challenge rules). Ground-truth semantics are used during training and in some analysis tables.

numbers_note: Test-std results exist only for rows 1, 4 and 6; the other variants (4-Action + RedNet FT 33.1/6.89, 6-Action 30.8/7.60, 6-Action + Tether 26.6/9.79) are VAL only. Table 3 and Table A5 report ground-truth-segmentation results on 300-episode TRAIN/VAL subsets; for example, 6-Act reaches 58.0 SR / 16.9 SPL on VAL with GT segm. These tables disagree for the tethered agent's GT VAL numbers (52.2/26.0 in Table 3 vs 48.7/19.1 in Table A5). The coverage-prediction ablation SPL is printed as '8.7s7' (Table 2). Much of the analysis (failure modes, probes, curvature, fixed points) is reported only in figures.
results: On the Habitat 2020 ObjectNav TEST-STD split (MP3D), the 6-action RedNet-fine-tuned agent reaches 24.5% success, beating the previous best SemExp (17.9%, +37% relative) and the DD-PPO end-to-end baseline (6.2%). The tethered variant reaches 8.1% SPL versus 7.5 for SRCB-robot-sudoer (+8% relative). There is a large VAL-to-TEST drop (e.g. 34.4 to 19.9 SR for the 4-action agent), and with ground-truth segmentation the agents reach about 55-58% VAL success. This shows that segmentation quality is the dominant bottleneck.
limitations: Efficiency is low: exploration-reward agents wander near goals, so SPL stays around 6-10%. Tethered sparse-reward tuning raises SPL but lowers success and causes early 'quitting'.

Performance depends heavily on semantic segmentation. Training uses ground-truth MP3D semantics, and noisy, flickering RedNet predictions roughly halve success (especially for 6-action agents). The SGE feature injects the domain prior that the agent should go to the goal once seen.
Results vary widely between splits (large VAL vs TEST-STD gap, only 9 test scenes). The dynamics analysis is limited because the high-dimensional RNN fixed-point structure resists interpretation.
